backlogged.summary: featureTestFiles checks lstat only on the leaf path. This is safe because git tracks a symlinked directory as a single symlink entry, so no file path is listed beneath it. If the file list ever came from a source that expands directories, a symlinked parent directory in the working tree would need its own check.

overlayFiles runs fs.statSync(src) after the exclusive write, and does so once per file. The mode could be read once alongside the content, and a file that disappears between the lstat filter and the copy would surface as an io error. This is only a minor race and not a real problem for a cooperative builder.

The vacuity failure message differs depending on whether an overlay was applied ('with the feature's test files' or not). Both variants contain 'already passes on base', so AC-1 holds. Consumers that match the full message text would need to know about both variants.
verify.test_count is unset in this repository, so the verify run warns that a test-count decrease is not checked. Setting it in .harness/config.json would give the project this protection.
The isTestPath alias in lib/glob.mjs is a thin wrapper over matchesAnyGlob. It adds a second name for the same function without adding behaviour, and could be dropped or documented as intentional.

featureTestFiles checks lstat only on the final path, not its parents. Scenario: base tracks test/a.test.mjs, and the feature replaces the test/ directory with a symlink to an outside directory that also contains a.test.mjs. `git diff --name-only` still lists test/a.test.mjs (as deleted), and lstat(top/test/a.test.mjs) follows the parent symlink and reports a regular file. The outside file's content is then copied into the temporary base worktree. SC-2 covers only a test path that is itself a symlink, so this is not a blocking defect, and the impact is low: the head-side run already executes through the link and the base worktree is removed afterwards. Hardening: skip a path when any parent segment under `top` is a symlink, or when realpath(src) is outside `top`.

overlayFiles copies file mode bits with `statSync(src).mode & 0o777`, which can include group/other write bits from the working tree. This is harmless in a temporary worktree; masking with 0o755 would be tidier.
The overlay is unbounded: a very large or very numerous set of changed test files is read fully into memory and copied. This is not a trust-boundary issue under threat model D1.
